hook: Hold your position in a lively German debate like a seasoned panellist: graded claims, exact collocations, fair reporting and calm steering.
intro: The closing conversation of this module, in your own AI assistant with voice on: a discussion on an economic or media question in which you hold a position with stylistic control. Copy the exercise in, say ‘Los geht’s’, answer in full sentences; the score and corrections come at the end. The tutor listens for six things: every claim graded with an adverb (durchaus, keineswegs, geradezu, immerhin); collocations instead of generic verbs (Kritik üben, Maßnahmen ergreifen); the other side’s position reported in the Konjunktiv I; one rhetorical touch — a qualified concession, a litotes or a rhetorical question — rather than a flat verdict or a folksy saying; a clean register shift when the tutor changes tone; and the moderator’s moves (zuspitzen, festhalten, zusammenfassen) when the tutor asks you to steer. This is a real debate in rehearsal — the kind you have at work, on a panel or over dinner.
tips[0].title: Grade every claim
tips[0].text: durchaus (certainly), keineswegs (by no means), geradezu (downright), immerhin (at least), ohnehin (in any case), ausgesprochen (decidedly). One per sentence, placed before the adjective or the verb it grades.
tips[0].check.why: durchaus affirms a claim against an expected doubt: certainly worth reading. keineswegs would deny it, and ohnehin means 'anyway'.
tips[1].title: Collocation, not generic verb
tips[1].text: Maßnahmen ergreifen (not machen), Kritik üben (not geben), eine Rolle spielen, Verantwortung übernehmen, eine Entscheidung treffen. A native listener hears the difference immediately.
tips[1].check.why: The fixed pair is Kritik üben. Kritik geben or machen sounds like a translation from English.
tips[2].title: Report the other side in the Konjunktiv I
tips[2].text: Before you answer a position, restate it at a distance: Die Befürworter argumentieren, … sei / habe / werde … Keep the Konjunktiv for every clause of the report, then switch to the indicative for your own view.
tips[2].check.why: The Konjunktiv I carries every clause of the report, so the second verb is helfe too. hilft would make the claim your own.
tips[3].title: Concede with a qualification; understate with a litotes
tips[3].text: Instead of a flat verdict: a qualified concession (Zugegeben, …, aber … · So berechtigt der Einwand ist, so wenig trifft er den Kern), a litotes (nicht unerheblich, alles andere als, nicht ohne), or a rhetorical question (Wer wollte ernsthaft bestreiten, dass …?). One touch per turn is mastery; a proverb or a string of sayings sounds folksy in a serious discussion.
tips[3].check.why: A litotes denies the opposite: nicht unerheblich means 'considerable', said with restraint. The other two say the risks are small.
tips[4].title: Shift register on request
tips[4].text: When the tutor switches tone, rebuild the whole sentence in the new register and signal it if you like (salopp gesagt, um es mal locker zu sagen); then return just as cleanly.
tips[4].check.why: A register shift rebuilds the whole sentence in everyday words. The other two stay formal.
tips[5].title: Steer as well as argue
tips[5].text: Um es zuzuspitzen: … · Lassen Sie uns festhalten, dass … · Ich fasse zusammen: … — the moderator’s moves show control of the whole exchange, not just your turn.
tips[5].check.why: The summing-up move is zusammenfassen: Ich fasse zusammen. Festhalten and zuspitzen are different moves and don't combine with zusammen.
remember[0]: durchaus / keineswegs / geradezu / immerhin: grade, don’t just claim.
remember[1]: Collocations; the other side in Konjunktiv I; one concession or litotes per turn — no proverbs.
remember[2]: Switch register whole; steer with zuspitzen, festhalten, zusammenfassen.
exam: Holding a position with control of style and register is what the C2 exam discussion asks for — and what any serious debate at work demands.
